blurb: `select[T]` and `firstAs[T]` read each row into the record `T`, matching columns to fields by name, so every field needs a column of that name. `Json.decodeSql` reads a literal `all` or `first` the same way, for each required field. Rename the field, or alias the column in the SQL (`… AS price`) so the names agree.
summary: A record read from a literal D1 statement has a field with no column of that name. For a `select[T]` / `firstAs[T]` row type, the column list the compiler writes from `T` does not prepare against the schema the binding's migrations build; for a `Json.decodeSql[T]` of the rows of a literal `all` / `first`, a required (non-`Option`) field of `T` has no result column.
